input.recap: JusPrin's tool registry defines 39 tools. 29 of them are exposed over MCP and 10 are not. Nothing was changed.

content.text:
The project has 39 tools, and 29 of them are exposed over MCP. All 39 are defined in one table in [ToolRegistry.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1020). Each tool carries a flag that says where it can be used: the in-app project chat, the MCP server, or the printer panel's own chat. The MCP server lists and accepts only tools with the MCP flag, in [McpProtocol.cpp:196](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp:196) and [McpServer.cpp:105](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpServer.cpp:105).

The live JusPrin MCP server connected to this session confirms it: it offers exactly those 29 tools.

**Available both in the app and over MCP (28):** activity_cancel, calibration_generate, export_file, object_analyze, object_divide, object_divide_preview, object_merge, object_place, object_repair, plate_layout, presets_list, print_dialog_open, printer_list, printer_setup, printer_setup_preview, project_attachment_read, project_delete_items, project_open, region_annotate, settings_apply_patch, settings_get, settings_preview_patch, settings_search, slice_inspect, slice_report, slice_start, view_render, workspace_inspect.

**MCP only (1):** object_import_file. It imports a model from a file path. In the app, the matching tool is object_import, which takes a file the person attached to the chat instead.

**Not on MCP (10):**
- **In-app project chat only (3):**
  - object_import imports a file attached in chat. An MCP client has no chat attachments, so it uses object_import_file.
  - setup_record writes the setup card in the project chat.
  - skill_read reads skills that the Agent page sends with the request. It is offered only when at least one such skill was sent.
- **Printer panel chat only (7):** printer_identify, printer_add, printer_change, printer_connection_status, printer_host_connect, printer_bambu_connect, issue_report_open. A code comment says these are kept out of the project chat because it "has no printer panel to draw a card in". They are also left off MCP.

My guess is that the setup-card and printer-panel tools are left off MCP because their results are drawn as cards in JusPrin's own chat UI, which an outside MCP client doesn't have. I took that from the code structure. I didn't find a comment or commit message that says so.
how important is it for us to make sure the tools/mcp tools are as future-proof as possible? any backard compatibility issues you can think of?

input.recap: I found two places where changing a tool can break something that already exists: projects with saved chats, and outside AI agents connected over MCP. I haven't tested what happens when an old chat names a tool that no longer exists. Nothing was changed.
input.ask: Should I test what happens when an old saved chat names a tool that was removed?

content.text:
It matters, but for two reasons that are less obvious than "an outside agent calls a tool by its old name." Tool names, arguments and error codes are a contract in two places: inside project files that people have saved, and in whatever people have built around the MCP server. Outside agents themselves are the least fragile part.

**Where a change is cheap.** Outside agents don't hard-code the tool list. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor ask the app for its tools each time they start a session, so a renamed tool simply shows up under its new name. The in-app chat is the same: the app, its page and its prompt ship together, and the model gets the current list on every request.

**Where a change can break things:**

1. **Saved chats inside project files.** Someone chats with the AI, which calls `object_place`, and saves the project. Months later they open it in a newer app where that tool was renamed. The chat history keeps each tool call raw, with its name and arguments, and sends it back to the model as it is ([RecordConversion.cpp:31](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/RecordConversion.cpp:31)). I haven't verified what Anthropic, OpenAI or DeepSeek do when the history names a tool that the current request doesn't offer. It might be harmless, or the request might be rejected and the chat stop working. Projects must open in later versions, so this is the riskiest of the four.

2. **Things people build around the MCP server.** In Claude Code, a person might allow `mcp__jusprin__settings_apply_patch` to run without asking each time, or write their own skill or script that names tools and fields. A rename quietly breaks those: the permission no longer matches, and the script calls a tool that's gone. The error codes (`stale_workspace`, `needs_step` and so on) belong to the same contract, because the server's instructions tell outside agents what to do for each one.

3. **The app and the bridge disagree on a version.** `jusprin-mcp` is the small helper program that outside agents launch, and it passes their calls to the running app. The app accepts exactly one protocol version from it, `2026-07-28`, and rejects anything else ([McpProtocol.cpp:156](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp:156)). Both ship in the same install, so they normally agree. They can disagree after an update: the old app is still running, and the new helper on disk talks to it. Today the helper only logs that the versions differ. If that version is ever bumped, the mismatched pair fails until the app is restarted.

4. **The helper's path is written into other apps' settings.** Setting up a connection writes the full path of `jusprin-mcp` into files like `~/.claude.json`. Moving or renaming the helper breaks every connection that was already set up. On Linux the path written is the AppImage file itself. My guess is that downloading a new AppImage with a different file name leaves the old path behind, but I haven't checked.

**What already protects you.** [test_tool_registry.cpp:70](tests/agent/test_tool_registry.cpp:70) pins the exact list of tool names for MCP and for the in-app chat, so a rename fails a test and shows up in review. Nothing pins the arguments or the error codes in the same way.

**How important, overall.** That depends on whether the MCP server has shipped to users yet, and I couldn't tell from the repo. If it hasn't, renaming now costs nothing. After the first release I'd suggest these rules (proposals, not agreed): add new arguments only as optional ones; rename a tool only while keeping the old name working as an alias; never remove an error code; and give the app-to-helper protocol at least a one-version overlap before bumping it. Saved chats need those rules either way, because projects with chats already exist on this branch.
Yes, test it

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

The search turned up consistent evidence that a Streamable HTTP server should answer an unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` with HTTP 400, though most results are SDK code, PRs, or third-party docs rather than the official spec.

- **Core rule:** The spec requirement appears in several sources. One SDK pull request quotes it directly, and MCP 2025-11-25 requires servers to respond with 400 Bad Request when receiving a request with an invalid or unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version header.
- **Missing header:** Missing headers are treated differently. One source says if not provided, server SHOULD assume 2025-03-26 for backwards compatibility, and a C# SDK issue notes that a missing header is allowed for backwards compatibility.
- **Error body:** Implementations commonly return a JSON-RPC error. One Python SDK example shows a 400 whose message names the unsupported value and lists supported versions (HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request with a message stating the unsupported protocol version and the supported versions).
- **Newer spec (2026-07-28):** A Zuplo glossary describes a stricter model in which an unsupported version is rejected with 400 and UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. A Korean-language guide says the same, returning HTTP 400 Bad Request along with a list of versions the server supports.
- **Caution on status codes:** One draft-spec mirror warns that a 400 is also used by modern servers for UnsupportedProtocolVersionError, MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError, and header-validation failures, so the status alone does not indicate that a version fallback should happen, so clients should inspect the body.
- **Known implementation issues:** A Python SDK discussion reports that StreamableHTTPServerTransport._validate_protocol_version() treats this as a literal string and returns 400 Bad Request, even when supported versions are present in the list when clients send comma-separated values. A Ruby SDK change merged in May 2026 fixed a server that was not reading the header at all, accepting any value.

Caveat: I did not reach the official spec pages directly. The 2026-07-28 details come from secondary sources, so verify them against modelcontextprotocol.io before relying on them.

All four accepted it with HTTP 200 and replied normally: OpenRouter gpt-5.4-mini, OpenRouter deepseek-v4-flash, OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, and Anthropic claude-opus-5-5 (Anthropic request hand-converted the way RecordConversion.cpp does). The chat page shows cards from the saved `title`, not a name table, so an unknown name just gets no special card. The only throw is `bring_tools` in ProviderAgent.cpp, for a skill naming a tool the build lacks. Skills ship with the app, so that case is a build error.

content.text:
Renaming or removing a tool won't break chats people have already saved, so I'm dropping that from the list of risks. And I didn't remove the version check: the strict check is in the app, not the bridge, and it has a real reason to exist.

**The saved-chat test.** I used a real request the app logged on Nov 5: a printer chat where the AI had called `printer_connection_status` and `printer_bambu_connect`. I sent it to each provider twice. The first copy was unchanged, as a control. The second had those two tools removed from the tool list, while the history still showed the AI calling them. That second copy is what a newer app would send for an old chat after those tools were removed or renamed.

| Provider and model | Unchanged | Tools removed |
|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter, gpt-5.4-mini | accepted, normal reply | accepted, normal reply |
| OpenRouter, deepseek-v4-flash | accepted, normal reply | accepted, normal reply |
| OpenAI, gpt-5.4-mini | accepted, normal reply | accepted, normal reply |
| Anthropic, claude-opus-5-5 | accepted, normal reply | accepted, normal reply |

In every case the model just said the printer was connected, as it should. The 8 requests used about 170k input tokens in total.

The app's own code handles an unknown tool name too. Every place that looks up a saved tool call by name checks for a missing tool and moves on. The chat page draws each card from the title saved with it, so an old tool just shows no special card.

What I didn't cover:
- I didn't open an old project in the real app and keep chatting. I sent the app's logged request myself, changing only the tool list and turning streaming off.
- The log only had OpenRouter-format requests, so I built the Anthropic one by hand, following the app's converter in `RecordConversion.cpp`.
- I didn't test a tool that keeps its name but changes its arguments. I'd expect that to be fine too, because providers didn't check the old calls against any tool definition here. That's an inference, not a test.

**The version check.** There are two checks, and neither belongs to the bridge in a way that needs removing:
- **The bridge** compares its version with the app's and only writes a log line when they differ. It blocks nothing, and it's the only clue in the log when a mismatched pair misbehaves, so I left it in.
- **The app** rejects any protocol version other than `2026-07-28` ([McpProtocol.cpp:156](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp:156)). That string names the message format the bridge and the app use with each other. Rejecting a version it doesn't know is what the MCP spec asks of an HTTP server, and it turns a format mismatch into a clear error. Without it, a future format change would be misread quietly. Removing it would change nothing today, since the version has never changed, but it would hide that future mismatch.

The real gap is a missing fallback, not the check. The bridge already asks the app which versions it supports, so when the version is bumped, the fix is for the app to also accept the previous version for one release. That isn't needed until a bump happens.

I saved the test result to memory so a later session doesn't repeat it. The test script is at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/9c09cf48-29be-44df-866a-6ba06c17fed7/scratchpad/replay_removed_tool.py`.

input.recap: The riskiest area is JusPrin's own project store. Every saved project lives there, each file accepts exactly one format version, and none has migration code. Old apps calling the JusPrin server come second. I read the code but didn't test an upgrade.
input.ask: Should I add migration hooks and an old-project test to the project store now?

content.text:
The riskiest area is how JusPrin saves projects, not the AI tools. Every saved project lives in a JusPrin-only store, every file in it accepts exactly one format version, and none of it has migration code. Today that's fine, because the code says JusPrin v2 "is not live yet". After the first release, it means the first format change can lock people out of every project they saved.

Ranked, riskiest first. I read the code for all of these and tested none of them with a real upgrade.

**1. The local project store (high).** When someone presses Cmd+S, JusPrin saves a version into `jusprin/projects/<id>/` in the app's data folder, not into the 3MF they opened. That folder holds a `HEAD` file (format 1), one record per version (format 1), and `current-state.json` (format 2). Inside that file is the project document (format 1), which holds the chats, tool calls, print records and region labels. Each loader accepts its exact number and nothing else ([ProjectStateDocument.cpp:544](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:544), [ProjectVersionStore.cpp:600](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:600)).

What the person sees after a format bump: they update, click a recent project, and opening fails with "managed project state is invalid" ([ProjectPersistence.cpp:405](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:405)). The same happens if they go back to an older version. The failure is loud, which is good, but every project is affected.

Two smaller points in the same area:
- The store builds its files with OrcaSlicer's 3MF writer and lays each object out under a name built from Orca's internal backup number. My guess is that a future upstream release could change that layout, but I haven't checked whether Orca treats it as stable.
- A 3MF from someone else that carries an older project document is handled more quietly. The app renames that part to `.corrupt` and starts the chat history fresh.

**2. Old apps calling a newer JusPrin server (medium to high).** Installed apps keep calling the server's chat endpoint, model list, sign-in, account and credits, and print reports, and you can't update the apps in the field. Every change on the server has to keep working with every version you've shipped. The app already copes with one case: a model served in a format it doesn't speak is simply skipped. Nothing in this repo checks the rest; it depends on discipline on the server side.

**3. The MCP server for outside AI agents (medium, after release).** This is the contract from earlier: tool names, arguments, error codes, and the helper program's path written into other apps' settings files. Saved chats are not part of the risk, as the test showed.

**4. Things inherited from OrcaSlicer (low to medium).** Exported 3MFs carry no JusPrin data, so OrcaSlicer opens them normally. Printer and material profiles are ordinary Orca presets. Here the risk comes from each upstream release you merge and from the fork's own edits inside Orca's files, which the stewardship rules already cover.

**5. Small things (low):**
- The app's own settings keys, such as `jusprin_agent.*`.
- `printer_facts.json` (format 1).
- The file outside agents use to find the running app, which is rewritten at every launch.
- The messages between the app and its web pages, which always ship together.

**What I'd propose before the first release (not agreed):**
- Give each store file a loader that upgrades older formats step by step.
- Have the app refuse a newer format with a message saying the project was made by a newer JusPrin.
- Commit a project store saved by each release as a test file, with a test that the next build opens it.
Not now

Here's what the search turned up. The sources are mostly practitioner blogs and forum posts, so treat them as experience reports rather than standards.

**Additive changes are the safe default.** One guide notes that a new version is unnecessary when newer code can already handle what older versions send, and that extra optional query parameters usually don't need a version bump (Educative). The reverse direction is the risk: a restructured field, such as turning a string into an object, makes old parsers crash (Educative).

**Plan for clients you can't update.** A mobile app can stay installed for months, so you can't force every user onto the latest contract overnight (Capgo). Another guide suggests making the version rule server-side with a default, then requiring clients to send the new value once most users have upgraded (AppMaster). A forum thread on client-driven versioning argues that new clients should hit updated endpoints directly while old clients go through compatibility layers (Reddit snapshot).

**Long support windows and clear deprecation.** One team's internal plan proposes supporting at least two API versions at once, a minimum of six months for the previous version, and a dashboard showing active client versions (Kordant task doc). Twitter's v1.1 endpoint stayed up roughly a year after its v2 release, which gave developers time to migrate (Educative).

**Forced upgrade.** The sources I found don't describe minimum-supported-version gates or forced-upgrade mechanisms in detail. The closest point is that a staged rollout can't handle backward-incompatible changes, because end users can't be forced to upgrade (Educative). That suggests a minimum-version check (for example, returning an "upgrade required" response below a threshold) is the usual escape hatch, but I'd verify this against a dedicated source before relying on it.

**Practical takeaways:** keep changes additive, make the version visible on every request, publish a written deprecation policy with a long sunset window, and track which client versions are still active before retiring anything.

input.recap: The project store can already take new fields, but four exact-match version numbers and two strict value lists would turn most changes into a lockout. Server requests carry OrcaSlicer's version, not JusPrin's. No code changed.
input.ask: Should I make server requests carry JusPrin's own version?

content.text:
Short answers: the project store's readers are mostly flexible already, but four exact-match version numbers would turn even safe changes into a lockout. On the server question, versioning the API is common and you already have it (`/ent/jusprin/v2/…`), but on its own it isn't enough. The bigger gap is that the server can't tell which JusPrin release is calling it. I read the code for both; nothing is changed or tested.

**1. Can the project store take foreseeable changes without breaking?**

What already copes well:
- The project document, which holds the chats, tool calls and print records, is kept as raw JSON and edited in place. If a newer build adds a field and an older build later edits the project, that field survives.
- Most fields are read with a default when missing: 188 reads use a default, and only 13 require the field.
- Version records are written once and never edited, and readers ignore fields they don't know.

How each likely change fares today:

| Change | Today |
|---|---|
| Add a field to a chat, tool call or print record | Fine, as long as nobody bumps a version number |
| Add a tool-call state (say "waiting") or source (say "printer") | An older build throws when it reads that chat ([ProjectStateDocument.cpp:58](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:58), [:373](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:373)) |
| Add a message state or print destination kind | An older build quietly misreads it: an unknown message state becomes "complete", and an unknown destination becomes "export" |
| Rename or remove a field | Breaks; version records require every field |
| Store part of the model somewhere new | An older build would ignore the new field and open an incomplete model without saying so |

The main blocker is that each of the four store files carries one number that means "the only format I accept". There's no way to say "older builds may read this" apart from "older builds must not read this". Git separates the two: its repository format version is paired with named extensions that older Git refuses only when it doesn't know them.

Proposal (not agreed):
- An additive change never bumps the number.
- A build refuses only a number higher than it knows, and says the project was made by a newer JusPrin.
- Older numbers get migrated.
- An unknown state or kind is read as "unknown" and shown plainly, instead of throwing or turning into a wrong value.

That covers everything in the table except the incomplete-model case. That one needs a real bump, so an older build refuses the project instead of opening a broken model.

**2. Is versioning the server API the common fix?**

It's part of it. Versioning covers changes that would break old apps, by running the old and new versions side by side. Most practitioner advice puts these first:
- Keep changes additive within a version.
- Know which client versions still call you.
- Publish how long old versions keep working.
- Have a way to tell an old app to update.

Two findings here:
- **The server can't see JusPrin's version.** Every chat, sign-in and account request goes through OrcaSlicer's HTTP class, which sends `User-Agent: JusPrin/2.5.0` ([Http.cpp:212](src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:212)). That 2.5.0 is OrcaSlicer's version; JusPrin's own is 2.0.0 ([Version.hpp:14](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp:14)). Only the update check sends the real one. So the server can't count which JusPrin releases are still in use, or treat one differently.
- **The app has no "please update" response.** I found nothing that handles a reply meaning "this version is no longer supported". It has to be in the first release, because an app already installed can't learn it later.

Sources:
- [Capgo: API versioning strategy](https://capgo.app/blog/api-versioning-strategy/)
- [AppMaster: API versioning for mobile apps](https://appmaster.io/blog/api-versioning-mobile-apps)
- [Educative: API versioning](https://www.educative.io/courses/grokking-the-api-design-interview-crash-course/my9253DgPPn)
- [DEV: Old apps still call home](https://dev.to/goodbarber/old-apps-still-call-home-38mk)
- [Kordant API versioning plan](https://git.freno.me/Mike/Kordant/src/branch/master/tasks/web-production/28-api-versioning.md)
Yes, do it

"""A stand-in JusPrin server that logs the method, path and User-Agent of every request."""
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

LOG = sys.argv[2]


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def record(self):
        with open(LOG, "a") as out:
            out.write(json.dumps({"method": self.command, "path": self.path,
                                  "userAgent": self.headers.get("User-Agent")}) + "\n")

    def reply(self, status, body, kind="application/json"):
        data = body.encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", kind)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/models"):
            self.reply(200, json.dumps({"data": [{"id": "slicer-1", "label": "Standard", "format": "responses"}]}))
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0))
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/responses"):
            events = [{"type": "response.completed", "response": {"id": "r-1", "status": "completed", "output": [
                {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok"}]}]}}]
            self.reply(200, "".join(f"event: {e['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(e)}\n\n" for e in events), "text/event-stream")
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    do_DELETE = do_GET

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()

The build is still running; it needs to rebuild most of the app, which takes about an hour at 4 jobs. The stand-in server and the scratch data folder are ready, so the end-to-end check runs as soon as the build finishes. Meanwhile, here are answers to your three questions.

**Do we still need a versioned API once requests carry JusPrin's version?**

Yes, keep both. They do different jobs, and the versioned API already exists: every server path is under `/ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- The path version is how you make a breaking change. You'd run `/v3/` next to `/v2/`, so installed apps keep using `/v2/` untouched.
- The version in each request tells you who is still on `/v2/`. Without it you can't know when it's safe to switch `/v2/` off, or treat a release with a known bug differently.

So nothing more needs versioning now. The missing piece is the one I mentioned earlier: a server reply the app understands as "this version is no longer supported, please update". It has to ship in the first release to be usable later.

**Do the two lists of project-store proposals overlap?**

Yes. They're the same plan, described once as rules for the format and once as the work to build it. Merged, it's five items:
1. An additive change never bumps the format number. This is only in the first list.
2. A build refuses a number higher than it knows and says the project was made by a newer JusPrin. This is in both lists.
3. Older numbers get migrated, step by step. This is in both lists.
4. A state or kind the build doesn't know is read as "unknown". This is only in the first list.
5. A project store saved by each release is committed as a test file, and a test checks that the next build opens it. This is only in the second list.

**Is there any reason not to do them?**

No reason not to, but each one has a cost:
- **Item 1 needs a judgment on every change.** The question each time is whether an older build, ignoring the new field, would do something wrong. If the answer is yes, the change must bump the number. The case that must bump is a newer build storing part of the model somewhere new, because an older build would open an incomplete model.
- **Item 2 means going back a version locks you out.** Someone who installs an older JusPrin can't open projects saved by a newer one after a bump. That's on purpose, because the alternative is quietly losing data.
- **Item 4 is about showing, not acting.** An older build may display "unknown" for a newer state, but must not act on it, for example by treating an unknown tool-call state as finished. Each place that shows these values needs a plain "unknown" display.
- **Items 3 and 5 add a release step.** Every bump needs a migration and its test kept forever, and every release needs its saved store committed as a test file.
- **Timing matters.** Before the first release this is cheapest, because nothing has to be migrated yet. After it, the first release's format is something you'll have to migrate from.
Go ahead with those items. commit to master branch for the server, and jusprin-dev branch for the app

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:
	•	--no-pager (e.g., git --no-pager log)
	•	or setting GIT_PAGER=cat (e.g., GIT_PAGER=cat git diff)

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.

"""The gateway's own error answers.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}} with text
from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed
out", so 401 means only that the person's own token was missing or rejected.
credits_exhausted adds what the client needs to offer a way on, beside "error".
"""
import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'credits_exhausted': 'You do not have enough credits for this message.',
    'text_too_short': 'A report needs a few sentences.',
    'photo_needed': 'A report needs a photo of the printed object.',
    'photo_unreadable': 'That photo could not be read.',
    'already_reported': 'This print already has a report.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',
    'rate_limited': 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)
from oauth2_provider.oauth2_backends import get_oauthlib_core


def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.
    """
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=[])
    if not valid or not oauthlib_request.user.is_active:
        return None
    return oauthlib_request.user

class GatewayEndpoint:
    # Bearer-token requests carry no CSRF token. Without this, a request that
    # reaches Django's request handling gets CsrfViewMiddleware's 403 instead
    # of the ImproperlyConfigured below, and never reaches Sentry.
    csrf_exempt = True

    def __init__(self, fmt: str):
        self.fmt = fmt

    def __call__(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        # Django only reaches this when the process does not serve
        # jusprin.v2.asgi (a WSGI worker, or a different ASGI_APPLICATION). A
        # deployment fault: let it reach Sentry rather than stream badly.
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(
            f'{request.path} must be served by the jusprin.v2.asgi application; '
            'it cannot stream from a Django view in this Django version')

    async def asgi(self, scope, receive, send):
        # Neither daphne nor channels opens a ThreadSensitiveContext, so without
        # this one every sync_to_async call below would run on asgiref's single
        # thread per process, behind every websocket consumer's database work.
        # Django's own ASGI handler opens one per request in the same way.
        async with ThreadSensitiveContext():
            # Django's own handler brackets every request with these signals;
            # they are what closes stale database connections.
            await sync_to_async(signals.request_started.send, thread_sensitive=True)(
                sender=self.__class__, scope=scope)
            try:
                await self._handle(scope, receive, send)
            finally:
                await sync_to_async(_finish_request, thread_sensitive=True)(self.__class__)

    async def _handle(self, scope, receive, send):
        async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            await self._handle_in(scope, receive, send, stack)

    async def _handle_in(self, scope, receive, send, stack):
        try:
            if scope['method'] != 'POST':
                raise GatewayError(405, 'method_not_allowed')
            user = await sync_to_async(_authenticate_scope, thread_sensitive=True)(scope)
            if user is None:
                raise GatewayError(401, 'unauthorized')
            headers = _headers(scope)
            turn_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-turn', '')
            request_kind = headers.get('x-jusprin-request', '')
            chat_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-chat')
            if not TURN_ID.match(turn_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Turn header is missing or not valid.')
            if request_kind not in REQUEST_KINDS:
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Request header must be reply, title or note.')
            if chat_id is not None and not capture.CHAT_ID.match(chat_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Chat header must be 32 lowercase hex digits.')
            large = await stack.enter_async_context(_large_request_slot(scope))
            raw_body = await _read_body(receive, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_MAX_BODY_BYTES)
            if raw_body is None:
                return  # the client left before sending the whole body
            if large or len(raw_body) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_LARGE_BODY_BYTES:
                # Parsing and re-encoding megabytes of JSON takes long enough
                # to stall every websocket this process serves.

async def _wait_for_disconnect(receive):
    while (await receive())['type'] != 'http.disconnect':
        pass


async def _send_error(send, error: GatewayError):
    await send({'type': 'http.response.start', 'status': error.status, 'headers': [
        (b'content-type', b'application/json'),
        (b'cache-control', b'no-store'),
    ]})
    await send({'type': 'http.response.body', 'body': error.body(), 'more_body': False})

class WebLinkTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # The pages are drawn in the host's syndicate's brand.
        base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        base.sites.add(Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})[0])
        Site.objects.clear_cache()
        # The cached site would outlive this test's rolled-back rows.
        self.addCleanup(Site.objects.clear_cache)
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'link-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def ask(self, body, token=None):
        return Client().post(URL, json.dumps(body), content_type='application/json',
                             HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token or self.token}')

    def link(self, body):
        response = self.ask(body)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
        return response.json()['url']

    def test_a_wrong_token_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ask({'page': 'prices'}, token='not-a-token').status_code, 401)

    def test_with_no_token_it_is_credits_and_plans_as_a_guest(self):
        for page in ('prices', 'billing'):
            response = Client().post(URL, json.dumps({'page': page, 'from': 'welcome'}), content_type='application/json')
            self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
            self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1&from=welcome')
        response = Client().post(URL, '{}', content_type='application/json')
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1')

    def test_a_body_that_is_not_an_object_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(Client().post(URL, 'nope', content_type='application/json',
                                       HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}').status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.ask(['prices']).status_code, 400)

    def test_the_link_signs_in_and_goes_to_the_page_with_where_the_click_was(self):
        url = self.link({'page': 'billing', 'from': 'account'})
        self.assertTrue(url.startswith('http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/open/'))

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

"""A stand-in JusPrin server that logs the method, path and User-Agent of every request."""
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

LOG = sys.argv[2]


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def record(self):
        with open(LOG, "a") as out:
            out.write(json.dumps({"method": self.command, "path": self.path,
                                  "userAgent": self.headers.get("User-Agent")}) + "\n")

    def reply(self, status, body, kind="application/json"):
        data = body.encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", kind)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/models"):
            self.reply(200, json.dumps({"data": [{"id": "slicer-1", "label": "Standard", "format": "responses"}]}))
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0))
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/responses"):
            events = [{"type": "response.completed", "response": {"id": "r-1", "status": "completed", "output": [
                {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok"}]}]}}]
            self.reply(200, "".join(f"event: {e['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(e)}\n\n" for e in events), "text/event-stream")
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    do_DELETE = do_GET

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

The app follows the macOS appearance, not `dark_color_mode`; for dark captures deliver an `appearance: dark` envelope to the page and reapply it after any full `state` (a chat turn resends it). A stand-in provider (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` → local server that hangs while a flag file exists, else answers 401) produces "checking" and "rejected" for real.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. - An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

---
name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

result.output:
makes.

Tests and their build
- load_files() no longer takes strings; the harnesses pass paths.
- Includes that 2.5.0's headers stopped providing are named directly.
- libslic3r_gui embeds Python now: tests/jusprin_support/PythonRuntime.cmake
  copies the runtime beside each fork test that links it, as OrcaSlicer's
  one nozzle per extruder first asks about nozzle changing.
- The smooth timelapse, support interface and layer height questions are
  reworded; the layer height one names the limit it adjusts to, the
  upper one first, as check_layer_height does.
- The save-time temperature check writes degrees as a single ℃.

The workspace harness compares every forwarded question with what
OrcaSlicer asks by hand; it now expects the clumping question in the
case that gained it and OrcaSlicer's reworded bed temperature slice
error. It also hands a percent setting's handler the number a percent
field gives, which 2.5.0's new wipe retraction handlers read.

## Shell: answer 2.5.0's offer to migrate filament presets with "Don't remind me again"

At startup, OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 offers to give user filament presets the printers
their system parent listed in 2.4.2. It counts every preset that takes its
printers from its parent as made before 2.5.0, because the preset file says
nothing about when it was made. 2.5.0 itself saves presets that way, so the
offer also lists presets made in 2.5.0. JusPrin has no presets from before
2.5.0, so in JusPrin the offer named presets JusPrin had just made, such as
a calibration's "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C · PA calibrated". The dialog names
OrcaSlicer and points to Help > Migrate Filament Presets, which JusPrin's menus
don't show.

The shell now stores the dialog's "Don't remind me again" answer, as it already
stores answers to OrcaSlicer's other startup questions. The change touches
only JusPrin files.

The dialog was also behind the workspace harness's heap corruption at exit
(0xC0000374). The harness ran inside the dialog's modal loop and then deleted
the main window, which owned the dialog, while the dialog's stack frame was
still live.

Not covered: OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 filament presets brought in by File > Import >
Import from OrcaSlicer can still lose printers their parent listed in 2.4.2,
and nothing offers to add them back.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Server version check and project store formats: name the release, refuse what is newer

Requests to the JusPrin server now name the JusPrin release, and the app
shows the server's own words when the server says that release is too old.
Local projects saved by a newer JusPrin are refused with a message to
update, instead of failing as broken files.

Release in every request
- Updates::user_agent() is "JusPrin/<JusPrin version> OrcaSlicer/<Orca
  version>". Orca's Http default sends "JusPrin/<Orca version>", which is
  the same for every JusPrin release built on one Orca release.
- It is sent by the JusPrin provider profile (chat, model list, account,
  account deletion), cloud sign-in, the web-link request, print reports
  and the update check. The OAuth token exchange still runs inside Orca's
  OAuthJob and keeps Orca's User-Agent.

Update required
- The server answers a release below its minimum with 426 and code
  update_required (tsd-enterprise, web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_version.py).
  update_required() in CloudAccount turns that into a non-retryable
  AgentError carrying the server's message. Chat turns, the sign-in check
  and the email sign-in use it.

Project store formats
- Workspace/StoredFormat.hpp states the rule every store file follows: an
  additive change keeps the format number; a change an older build would
  misread raises it and adds a step that upgrades the previous number; a
  build reads every number from the file's first to its own and refuses a
  higher one.
- The project document, HEAD, version manifests and current-state.json
  go through it. A newer one throws NewerFormatError (LoadResult::Newer for
  the document). Opening such a project from Home or chat says "This
  project was saved by a newer version of JusPrin. Update JusPrin to open
  it." instead of "Try again". A newer state.json imported from a 3MF is
  kept beside it as .newer, as a broken one is kept as .corrupt.
- A tool action whose state or source a newer build added no longer makes
  the whole project fail to open: it is left out of the page and left as
  written.

Saved project test data
- tests/data/jusprin_project_store/2.0.0 holds a project this release
  saved (20 mm box, one chat turn). The workspace harness opens it, checks
  the model and chat, then raises its HEAD number and checks the open is
  refused with the update message while the open project stays open.

Tested
- agent_bridge_tests: 570 cases pass. The eight new tests fail when the old
  behavior is put back.
- Workspace harness: the ten new checks pass. The eleven failures it
  reports (second_model_dropped and the calibration identity checks)
  appear unchanged in runs from before this change.
- Real app against a local stand-in server: every request carried
  "JusPrin/2.0.0 OrcaSlicer/2.5.0"; with the stand-in answering 426, the
  chat reply failed with the server's message and no retry.
EOF
